raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The MUSA branch of `get_available_gpu_memory()` selects host available memory for integrated devices, then immediately overwrites it with `torch.musa.mem_get_info()`. The CUDA branch already keeps these alternatives separate.

The same conditional fix was proposed by @yinli-systems in the closed, unmerged #25415. This PR is limited to that memory query and adds regression coverage.

## Modifications

Put the device-memory query in `else`. Cover integrated/discrete devices with cache clearing enabled and disabled in the existing CPU-registered platform tests. The test checks both the returned GiB value and that the unused memory source is not queried.

## Accuracy Tests

Normal package imports, CPU-only Linux/Python 3.12, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py
pytest test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py -q
```

Direct invocation: 73 tests pass. Pytest: 73 tests and 25 subtests pass. On unchanged main with the new test, the two integrated-device subcases fail (`2.0 != 6.0`); discrete-device controls pass. Both arms emit the same 23 pytest warnings.

The MUSA device/memory boundaries are mocked; no MUSA hardware or model execution was performed. Dependencies are inherited, not a qualification of the complete official CI environment.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this fixes a memory-capacity query, not kernel or inference performance.

## Checklist

- [ ] Full repository pre-commit (not run). Changed files pass Ruff 0.15.1 checks/format; AST, registered-test validation and diff check pass.
- [x] Focused regression coverage in the existing registered CPU test.
- [x] No new public interface or documentation change needed.
- [x] No model-output or performance claim.

The review fix is pushed as 9f5bd64 and re-review is requested. The latest [MUSA gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38030083857/job/114149033731?pr=43398) stops at `Require run-ci label (optional)`; the PR currently has no labels. Could a maintainer add `run-ci` when appropriate so the hardware CI can run? The passing CPU mock regression does not replace native MUSA validation.

Checked the three root CI failures on `9f5bd64`:

- [CPU shard 11](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38030084096/job/114155366804): Python 3.10 lacks `TestCase.enterContext`; #43505 has now fixed this on main.
- [AMD stage A](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38030084102/job/114155387822): PyArrow import requires NumPy >=2, but the environment has 1.26.4.
- [NPU HiCache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38030083869/job/114155556855): stacked KV tensors hit `getattr(..., None) or ()` in `pool_host/mha.py`; the existing #43308 addresses this.

These failures are outside the MUSA memory branch changed here. No extra source changes or duplicate fixes added. The MUSA-specific tests were skipped, so I am not claiming native MUSA validation.

Updated in 9f5bd64 to `free_gpu_memory, _ = torch.musa.mem_get_info(gpu_id)`. The regression now uses device 3 and checks that the requested device is passed through.

With the new assertion, the original PR fails the two discrete-device subcases; the exact committed revision passes 73 platform tests and 25 subtests on Linux CPU with mocked MUSA boundaries. Repository-configured Ruff checks/format and diff checks pass. No native MUSA hardware validation is claimed.

detail.title: [Bugfix] Preserve available host memory for integrated MUSA devices

files.patch:
@@ -540,7 +540,8 @@ def get_available_gpu_memory(
             # available due to not including cache memory. So we use the system available
             # memory metric instead.
             free_gpu_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
-        free_gpu_memory, total_gpu_memory = torch.musa.mem_get_info()
+        else:
+            free_gpu_memory, _ = torch.musa.mem_get_info(gpu_id)
     elif device == "mps":
         from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.mlx.runtime import use_mlx

@@ -560,6 +560,42 @@ def test_common_device_helpers_handle_mps_inline(
                 common.get_device.cache_clear()
 
 
+class TestMusaAvailableMemory(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_integrated_and_discrete_memory_sources(self):
+        from sglang.srt.utils import common
+
+        gpu_id = 3
+        for integrated in (True, False):
+            for empty_cache in (True, False):
+                with self.subTest(integrated=integrated, empty_cache=empty_cache):
+                    musa = MagicMock()
+                    musa.device_count.return_value = 4
+                    musa.current_device.return_value = gpu_id
+                    musa.get_device_properties.return_value.is_integrated = integrated
+                    musa.mem_get_info.return_value = (2 << 30, 16 << 30)
+                    with (
+                        patch.object(torch, "musa", musa, create=True),
+                        patch.object(common.psutil, "virtual_memory") as host_memory,
+                        patch.object(common, "empty_device_cache") as clear_cache,
+                    ):
+                        host_memory.return_value.available = 6 << 30
+                        self.assertEqual(
+                            common.get_available_gpu_memory(
+                                "musa", gpu_id, empty_cache=empty_cache
+                            ),
+                            6.0 if integrated else 2.0,
+                        )
+                        if integrated:
+                            musa.mem_get_info.assert_not_called()
+                        else:
+                            musa.mem_get_info.assert_called_once_with(gpu_id)
+                            host_memory.assert_not_called()
+                        if empty_cache:
+                            clear_cache.assert_called_once_with(musa)
+                        else:
+                            clear_cache.assert_not_called()
+
+
 class TestPinMemoryAvailability(CustomTestCase):
     """Tests for common pin-memory helper dispatch through platforms."""
